questions.prompt: Are you allowed to raise, feed, or keep pigs in Franklin?
choices: Yes, if they stay in a fenced backyard
No, it is unlawful to raise, feed, or keep swine in the city
Yes, up to two pigs per household
questions.answer: No, it is unlawful to raise, feed, or keep swine in the city
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

It is unlawful to slaughter any animal or to maintain any slaughter house within the
               city. (Prior code § 90.02)

It is unlawful for any person to raise, feed or keep any swine within the city. (Prior code § 90.03)

Whoever violates any provision of this chapter for which no penalty is specified shall,
               upon conviction thereof, be subject to such penalties as are contained in Section 1.16.010 of this code. (Amended during 2005 codification; prior code § 90.99)

Sections:

As used in this chapter, the following words are defined as follows: "Owner" means a person having a right of property in a dog or who keeps or harbors
               a dog or who has it in his or her care or acts as its custodian or who knowingly permits
               a dog to remain on or about any premises occupied by him or her. "Person" means any individual, firm, association, joint stock company, syndicate,
               partnership or corporation. "Restraint" means the securing of an animal by leash or lead or confining it within
               the real property limits of its owner or agent. (Ord. 05-09 § 1)

All dogs shall be kept under restraint. (Ord. 05-09 § 2)

Any owner who violates any provision of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of
               twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for the first offense, with the fines increasing by an
               increment of five dollars ($5.00) for each subsequent offense within one year of the
               first offense, plus reasonable attorney fees and other costs of collection. (Ord. 05-09 § 3)

The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to dogs leading blind persons. (Ord. 05-09 § 4)

                  welfare. "Curfew" means a prohibition against any person walking, running, loitering, standing,

               the corporate limits of the city, excepting persons officially designated to duty
